All five additions are now settled and recorded. Here's the **complete scope** for this first build, in plain terms:

**Core**
1. **Quick saving** — paste a link; title, description, icon, and preview fill in automatically; no duplicates.
2. **Your own touches** — edit the address, title, description, a note (light formatting), and tags (with suggestions from tags you've used).
3. **Read later** — mark links and view just those.
4. **Finding things** — search from simple words to exact `#tags`, `"phrases"`, and `and/or/not` logic; click a tag to filter.
5. **Ordering** — sort by newest, oldest, or title.
6. **Tidying** — archive (reversible) or permanently delete (confirmed).
7. **Holds up large** — one continuous, searchable list; long text trimmed.
8. **Graceful with problems** — rejects junk addresses, never loses a link, handles re-saving an archived one.
9. **Yours everywhere** — one private collection behind a simple sign-in, shared across your devices.

**The five you added**
10. **Bulk actions** — select many (or all matching a search) and tag / read-later / archive / delete together.
11. **Collections** — save a search as a named, always-live view.
12. **Preserved copies** — every new bookmark is auto-saved as a revisitable copy (the real PDF for PDFs), with a clear failure+retry, plus an optional per-bookmark Internet Archive copy.
13. **Import / export** — bring in a browser bookmarks file (folders become tags, dates kept) and export the standard bookmarks HTML.
14. **Settings** — default sort, list density, and text size, synced to your account.

**Recorded for a later round** (not this build): nothing outstanding right now.

**A couple of honest notes for building:** the preserved-copy capture and the Internet Archive submission rely on real backend/external services (only stand-ins in the prototype), so those are where actual-service availability matters.
